data.narrative: Completed Module 6 'Documentation' learning about documentation strategy (comprehensive vs minimal+links), writing on-call runbook with copy-pasteable commands, identifying three failures in flawed runbook (stale variable names, fake rollback command, missing Redis check), and fixing runbook with maintenance metadata and known failure modes table.

dimension_scores.observation: Identified three critical failures in flawed runbook (stale DB_CONNECTION_STRING vs DATABASE_URL, fake rollback command that rolls forward, missing Redis section) and explained impact on on-call engineer
dimension_scores.evidence: flawed_runbook_analysis.md contains detailed failure analysis with locations and fixes

dimension_scores.observation: Wrote runbook with copy-pasteable commands, no placeholders, numbered steps, tool prerequisites section, and constants section to eliminate duplication
dimension_scores.evidence: orderflow_runbook_fixed.md includes tool prerequisites and constants at top

dimension_scores.observation: Wrote runbook for on-call engineer at 3 AM - scannable under pressure, no assumed knowledge, all commands executable without interpretation
dimension_scores.evidence: orderflow_runbook_fixed.md uses numbered steps and copy-pasteable commands

dimension_scores.observation: Chose minimal+links documentation strategy, structured runbook with constants, prerequisites, health check, failure modes, escalation path, and known failure modes table
dimension_scores.evidence: orderflow_runbook_fixed.md has logical structure with clear headings

dimension_scores.observation: Added maintenance metadata (last verified date, review cadence) and known failure modes table to make runbook maintainable and useful for future incidents
dimension_scores.evidence: orderflow_runbook_fixed.md includes last verified, review cadence, and known failure modes table

strengths: Chose minimal+links documentation strategy with reasoning about tools staying current because people use them daily
Wrote runbook with copy-pasteable commands and no placeholders
Identified all three critical failures in flawed runbook
Fixed runbook with maintenance metadata and known failure modes table
data.recommendation: Apply 3 AM test to all future documentation - can someone follow it alone under pressure with no prior context? If not, it's not done

public_evidence.student_action: Wrote operational runbook with copy-pasteable commands, numbered steps for failure modes, escalation path, and rollback procedure
public_evidence.technical_detail: Runbook includes constants section, tool prerequisites, health check, 4 failure modes (database, Redis, worker, 5xx errors), escalation path, and known failure modes table
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Demonstrates ability to write documentation that works under pressure when systems are on fire - critical for on-call reliability

public_evidence.student_action: Identified three critical failures in flawed runbook (stale variable names, incorrect rollback command, missing Redis section) and corrected them
public_evidence.technical_detail: Fixed DB_CONNECTION_STRING to DATABASE_URL, replaced helm upgrade with helm rollback, added Redis/worker failure mode section with impact notes
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Shows ability to identify and fix documentation gaps that could cause incidents or extend recovery time

concepts_demonstrated.evidence: Added last verified date, review cadence, and update-on-change requirements to prevent stale documentation
